For me: 1. Lebron James 2. Anthony Davis 3. Stephen Curry 4. Kevin Durant 5. Russell Westbrook.

  1. ** Lebron James**- Although this man gets his fair share of hate, we all know that he is an elite player and a top ballot hall of famer. The dude averages 27.3 pts, 7.1 rbs, 6.3 asts along with 1.7 stls in his 13th season. Those are simply remarkable numbers. James is and has been consistent throughout his entire career. Although he had his ups and downs in the finals (Mavs) he also deserves the recognition of single-handedly carrying his Cavs (before his heat years) to the playoffs, and the finals.

  2. Anthony Davis- I know this might be debatable, but we can all agree Davis is a MONSTER. In terms of winning, Davis is far from the top, but his individual stats and his presence in the court is MVP material. For a guy who is 22, and averaging 19.5 Pts, 9.5 Rbs, 2,5 Blks, and 1.3 Stls a game, I think that is highly impressive. I personally think Davis has a more versatile, and a higher skill set than James,(Just a bit) but James is #1 simply b/c he's been in the league a lot longer. Davis added the 3 pointer to his arsenal, and is almost unstoppable on offense and on defense.

  3. Stephen Curry might be the best player in the world right now, but he gained that title very recently. From his rookie years, his numbers have been impressive, but does not surpass Davis or James. However, every NBA fan can agree. Stephen Curry is the best shooter that the NBA has seen. His release, & form is almost perfect, and everything shot he takes looks like it's going in. He has surpassed Miller and Allen in most 3pts made in a single season, and will eventually pass them in most 3pts made in NBA history. His play making skills are extraordinary, and he has been the cornerstone of that GSW team.

  4. Kevin Durant- Although he was injured last year, I think KD deserves to be in my top 5 list. He is 6'11, and he dribbles the ball like a point guard. His length makes his jump shots almost impossible to guard, and he can knock it from anywhere. He is almost unstoppable on offense. (No descriptions needed) He is also a very good defensive player, and has numbers very similiar to Brons. I felt like Durant would've continued his hall of fame performance last season, if not showing us his highest potential. If he was not injured last year, I definitely think he would be higher in my list.

  5. Russell Westbrook - I know many of you might wonder why I put Westbrook as my 5th best player. In my opinion, I feel like Westbrook has been overshadowed by Durant. The dude is ABSOLUTELY an Athletic freak. Even with Durant, Westbrook avgs 20-7-5. Without him, he avgs 26-10-7. (Almost a Triple-Double) Westbrook is simply a game changer due to his fast pace and athleticism, and can do almost everything that he is asked to do.
